about: Agent workload (build.py data.workload, src/model.js agent*, node report.js --workload, the page's Agents tab). A coding agent's turn first reads its fresh prompt tokens (the new part past the cached prefix, plus any part read again after a cache eviction), then decodes its answer. With F fresh prompt tokens per output token, a prefill rate P (prompt tok/s) and a decode capacity D (total tok/s of the agents decoding together), useful output is at most min(D, P / F). An engine whose long reads stop every decoding slot runs the two in turn, so it gets 1 / (F / P + 1 / D). The binding term is the smaller of D and P / F. A ledger row measured on a synthetic short-prompt load (one short prompt per agent, then decode only) measures D, decode capacity, never agent throughput. Every number here is {v, tag, src}.

many_agents_min.src: a setting: a recipe serving at least this many agents (recipe.conditions.workload.agents, else serving.batch) is a many-agent recipe; its throughput must rest on a real-agent ledger row of the same build, not only on synthetic short-prompt decode (check agent_workload)

build_key_re.src: a setting: the part of recipe.engine_build that names one engine build (a container image digest prefix); rows with the same key are the same build. A build string without it is its own key

real_kind.src: measured.workload_kind of a ledger row that replayed recorded agent conversations (prefixes byte for byte, recorded output lengths and tool gaps); its measured.agent_tps, prefill_tps, fresh_per_output and prefill_busy_pct are keyed cN like aggregate_tps

v: cold restarts: every agent's first prompt read cold inside the timed window (no warm-up)
evictions: a slot lent to another agent drops its cache, and the next turn reads the whole prompt again
template drift: the request renders an earlier turn differently, so the cached prefix stops matching early

replay_noise_pct.src: MEASURED: run-to-run noise of the 16-agent real-agent replay, two identical control runs of one build and env (ledger rows odie-fnx-iq3xxs-2xb70-real-ctl-n16-1026 and odie-fnx-iq3xxs-2xb70-real-ctl-r2-n16-1026): agent tok/s 33.4 vs 37.25 (|diff| / mean 10.9 %), turns per agent-minute 0.769 vs 0.845 (9.4 %), fresh prompt tokens per output 23.95 vs 19.84. A difference between two single replays smaller than this is inside noise; the report marks a MEASURED lever whose smallest measured gain is inside it

The replay client's count over its in-window turns (fresh_split.F of each row's replay result file, our lab notes, not published) reads 3.94-4.93 across the 17 steady-state 16-agent replays of 2026-10-26 (ledger rows tagged steady-state: odie-fnx-iq3xxs-2xb70-real-*-ss16-n16-1026* and odie-fnx-iq3xxs-2xb70-real-sp-m16-n16-1026); the trace needs 4.33 with a perfect cache (trace_ideal_fresh_per_output). The 16 earlier 16-agent replays of 2026-10-26, timed from a cold start, read 17.8-67.7 (cold first prompts and re-reads after cache evictions) and no longer set this profile

reads_stall_decode.src: XeStrata --batch-groups: a read longer than STRATA_BATCH_PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS (512) drains the pipe and every decoding slot waits until the read is done (generate.cpp); MEASURED in the engine log of the 16-agent replay: 76 reads, 446 s of prompt time in a 600 s window

v.lever: pipeline the two layer-split stages inside a batched read (several chunks per read)
refill the lent cache slots through pinned bounce buffers instead of one blocking pageable copy per slot
halve the ~1007 ms fixed cost of each read
v.src: INFERRED gain on a MEASURED decomposition: lab notes, prefill phase timing on the 16-agent replay control's engine log (75 reads over 512 tokens): a read costs ~1007 ms + 0.791 ms a token. Of the fixed part: parking the previous conversation 99 ms a read; giving the slot back 122 ms in 55 of the 75 reads (~83 ms a read); the batched read itself 614 ms + 0.8 ms a token; the remainder ~175 ms is INFERRED (checkpoint saves per stage and the 4-token header window). Copying the conversation into the slot takes another ~216 ms a read outside the read timing. The gain (halving the fixed part) is arithmetic, not yet measured

v.lever: share exact prompt prefixes across slots (STRATA_SHARED_PREFIX=1): cold subagents reuse the common system prompt start
v.src: MEASURED: two paired 16-agent real-agent replays on odie (2x B70, Flash-Next, one build, 600 s each). Run 1: shared prefix 39.46 agent tok/s and 0.845 turns per agent-minute against the control's 33.4 / 0.769 (ledger rows odie-fnx-iq3xxs-2xb70-real-sp-n16-1026, odie-fnx-iq3xxs-2xb70-real-ctl-n16-1026). Repeat: 40.46 / 0.896 against 37.25 / 0.845 (odie-fnx-iq3xxs-2xb70-real-sp-r2-n16-1026, odie-fnx-iq3xxs-2xb70-real-ctl-r2-n16-1026). Two-run means: agent tok/s +13 %, turns per agent-minute +8 %. The gain range is the agent tok/s ratio of each pair (x1.18, x1.09); replay noise between the two identical control runs was ~11 % in agent tok/s (settings.replay_noise_pct), so the repeat's +8.6 % alone is inside noise and the mean +13 % only just outside it. The lever lowers fresh prompt tokens per output (F 18.8 and 18.6 against 23.95 and 19.8) rather than raising the prefill rate P; the report applies the measured agent tok/s ratio as a factor on P, which moves the ceiling P / F by the same ratio

prefill_levers.src: INFERRED: lab notes, prefill floor analysis (arithmetic on the 76 measured reads, prompt_ms ~ 940 + 0.776 x tokens, and the code paths); each gain multiplies the prefill rate P, so a prefill-bound ceiling P / F rises by the same factor; not yet measured, except where a lever carries its own tag and src (shared_prefix: MEASURED)

prefill_pass.about: First-principles prefill (src/model.js prefillPass): a read of T fresh tokens runs in chunks of C tokens; each chunk makes one pass over the experts (almost every expert of every MoE layer is routed to when C x k >> E): the experts a card does not hold cross the PCIe link (less the share the CPU computes), the ones it holds are read once from VRAM. t(T) = ceil(T / C) x t_pass + T x m, t_pass = sum over the stages of nonresident bytes x (1 - cpu_share) / link + resident bytes / VRAM bandwidth, m = 2 x active params / (eta x card int8 ops). eta is the ONE fitted factor per engine (fit rows below); every other input is MEASURED, READ or INFERRED here. Attention and DeltaNet terms that grow with depth are left out (the model under-predicts the time of very long reads). P over an agent workload = mean read / (chunks per read x t_pass + mean read x m), over the read-size mix.

chunk_re.src: a setting: the engine flag that sets the prefill chunk; '--prefill auto' (no digits) keeps the engine's chunk_default. The last match wins

split_re.src: a setting: the layer-split boundary in the engine flags (stage 1 = layers below it, stage 2 = the rest, one card each)

cpu_share_re.src: a setting: the share of the nonresident experts the CPU computes instead of streaming them (strata prefill.cpp); assumed to overlap the PCIe stream
